hints.title: Use polynomial division
hints.body: Dividing a polynomial by a linear expression gives a polynomial quotient and a constant remainder. Choose a divisor that is zero at the input in the question.
hints.recap: A linear divisor leaves a constant remainder, which can be found by substitution.
hints.pitfall: A nonzero function value does not mean the divisor is a factor of the whole polynomial.
hints.pause: Write the division identity, substitute the given input and find the remainder.

recall.reminder: A linear divisor leaves a constant remainder, which can be found by substitution.

solution:
Write p(x)=(x−1)q(x)+r. Setting x=1 gives r=p(1)=2.

Thus p(x)=(x−1)q(x)+2 for some polynomial q. Answer A.
knowledgePattern: Remainder theorem as a logical deduction
